methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $7M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Navier, a seed-stage transportation company founded by Sampriti Bhattacharyya, has raised $7.2M to date. The transportation sector contains three private comparable companies (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride) and no public peers, limiting the applicability of traditional peer-median approaches for a narrow seed-stage cohort.

The primary applicable valuation method is stage-progression analysis. Using total raised ($7.2M) as a base proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to next-stage financing, this approach yields an implied valuation of $18M. The peer-median method is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the transportation sector—only one methodology provided reliable quantitative support for triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M to $21M, with a median point of $18M. This narrow range reflects dependence on a single applicable method rather than methodological triangulation; key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.5x multiplier for Navier's specific risk profile and stage, and the absence of true peer data to validate whether transportation-sector seed companies command premium or discount multiples relative to broader venture benchmarks.
